category: torrent index with a JSON service endpoint (bulk dataset plus search)

free_tier.stated: No key: /service/search?q=debian&size=2 returned JSON with infohash, name, size_bytes, seeders, leechers and completed. The HTML homepage is behind an Anubis proof-of-work challenge.

retention.stated: rows carry a scraped_date and are kept after the swarm dies; seeders is the liveness signal

egress.terms: no byte allowance: JSON only; whether the project also publishes a bulk dump was not checked on the pages read

interface_detail: /service/search?q=<query>&size=<n> returns JSON. The web front end is served behind Anubis v1.28.1, a proof-of-work challenge, which the API endpoint did not present to us.
tooling: One GET against /service/search. A bulk mirror would remove the query loop entirely, but the dump's existence and size were not verified today.
chaining: Search by title for a quick check, or take the bulk dump and filter locally; either way the infohash is what feeds a debrid cache check.

limits.value: none published; the front end answers a client without JavaScript with an Anubis proof-of-work challenge rather than a 429

limits_note: Anubis is a bot-defence layer, so the wall is computational rather than a quota: a browser solves it in seconds, a plain HTTP client does not.
binding_note: The HTML surface is the thing that breaks first, and it breaks on the challenge rather than on a rate; the JSON endpoint stayed open during the same session.

identity_cost.detail: No account for either surface. The HTML surface costs a proof-of-work computation, not an identity.

reliability_note: Anubis rejects clients that disable JavaScript features (the page names JShelter), and the front end and the service endpoint have different gates, so a pipeline tested on one can fail on the other.
confidence_note: Both surfaces were fetched on 2026-10-23: the JSON answered, the HTML returned the Anubis interstitial. A recorded run against the bulk dump would settle the dataset size.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200 application/json with infohash, name, size_bytes, seeders, leechers, completed and scraped_date
'Making sure you're not a bot!', Anubis version v1.28.1, proof-of-work challenge instead of the index

notes: Useful because the search endpoint is one GET with a stable schema, and the caveat is that the same host gates its HTML behind a proof of work, so an unannounced change would break a scraper without warning. The bulk-dump path that TorrentClaw's docs imply was not verified here.
